paper.title: VLCP: Vision Language Control Policy Closed-Loop Code Replanning for Robot Manipulation
paper.central_claim: A frozen VLM that writes the manipulation policy as a Python control function and re-observes (multi-view RGB, proprioception, state delta) and rewrites that function every K steps inside one episode, training-free and demonstration-free, lifts pooled success on a 57-task MuJoCo/RoboVerse (LIBERO) sweep from 3.5% (identical system queried once, K=T) to 35.1%; the gain is attributed to 27.3% within-episode recovery of failed grasps, at ~10 cache-warm VLM calls per episode, with a cross-episode skill library as a further contribution.
paper.claim_scope_note: Sim only (Franka, MuJoCo/RoboVerse), simulator-provided privileged object poses, GPT-5.5 as replanner, one episode per task.

signatures.object: Control function (Python, control(obs,J)->joint targets) written by a frozen VLM; baseline = same function written once per episode (K=T)
signatures.information: Per replan: two-view RGB (start and current of block), previous generated code and its K action dicts, JSON obs summary (EE pose, joints, privileged object poses), goal pin, skill library source. Hidden: no demonstrations, no fine-tuning. Privileged: simulator object poses and analytic Jacobian.
signatures.operation: Every K=50 steps (~10 per 500-step episode) re-query the VLM and replace the running control function
signatures.output: New control block (and optional skill modules) for the next ~K steps; within a block the compiled function still runs closed-loop on obs/J every step
signatures.conditions: Strong frontier VLM (GPT-5.5); small open models failed; simulator with resettable episodes; velocity-IK primitive supplied
signatures.feedback: Visual/numeric state at block boundary; previous code and action trace; no external verifier or success detector in the loop (task predicate only scores)
signatures.selection_rule_data: None: the newest block always replaces the old one; no accept/reject gate, no candidate sampling
signatures.persistence: Within episode: conversation history up to 20 pairs (images dropped from history copies)
signatures.claimed_effect: 3.5% -> 35.1% pooled success (57 tasks, single episode each); 27.3% failed-grasp recovery
signatures.failure_boundary: 40/55 episodes with failed grasp never recover; long-horizon Living-Room tasks 23.5%; latency 18.8 s per replan; untested on perception noise/real robot; K not swept

signatures.object: On-disk skill library of helper modules (control_policies/skills/)
signatures.information: VLM-authored helper modules from any replan; later prompts see up to 12 most recent module sources verbatim
signatures.operation: Extract labelled skill blocks, write atomically, import immediately; revert on import error and feed the error to the VLM at the next replan
signatures.output: Importable modules in subsequent control functions
signatures.conditions: Shared directory with process lock; library reset before each task in the main sweep
signatures.feedback: Import success only; no task-success filtering
signatures.selection_rule_data: Recency sort capped at 12; no promotion/curation criteria (authors explicitly drop Voyager-style curation)
signatures.persistence: Disk; across episodes and concurrent policy instances
signatures.later_use: Injected into Block B of every later replan
signatures.claimed_effect: Contribution 2: repertoire can grow without retraining (framed as outlook); no measured effect
signatures.failure_boundary: Stored code may be wrong; no verification of usefulness; no ablation

gap.author_gap: One-shot code-as-policy cannot recover from runtime errors; monitor/replan methods retry a fixed policy or reselect a subtask but do not rewrite the failing control code; VLAs need demonstrations and expose no reasoning point; the nearest controller-rewriting method rewrites only between trials.
gap.checked_gap: Real and concrete (a missed grasp carried silently to episode end; one-shot K=T gets 3.5%). However the exact design point is already occupied by concurrent CaP-Agent0 (authors concede), so the residual is a controlled ablation and recovery measurement rather than a new capability. Local card R05 (Act-Observe-Rewrite 2603.04466v1, rewrite between trials) supports the closest-neighbour description; neighbour full texts were not in the pinned input package, so the comparison rests on the authors' account plus that card.
gap.lineage: Code as Policies / ProgPrompt / ELLMER (one-shot code) -> Code-as-Monitor / DoReMi / Inner Monologue (monitor, retry, replan at task level) -> Act-Observe-Rewrite (rewrite between trials) -> VLCP / CaP-Agent0 (rewrite within episode)

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Step 1 responsibility boundary: VLM confined to writing the control program, IK/PD controller and Python interpreter execute exactly (partly present, boundary stated). Step 2 typed artifact: executable control function plus skill modules with a strict output contract (present). Step 3 close the loop with solver-verifiable output mid-construction: execution trace/action dict and re-observed state fed back at each block boundary (present; no external verifier of correctness). Step 4 ablate the feedback step to the undecomposed baseline: K=T (present). Step 5 cost accounting: calls, tokens, latency measured (present).
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: executable load-bearing artifact (met), single isolated mechanism whose removal returns to the one-shot baseline (met, K=T), loop driven by obtainable signals (met except privileged poses). Failure: assembly of off-the-shelf parts (partly: GPT-5.5 + IK + prompt), single-benchmark hand-tailored prompt (partly: prompt tuned to LIBERO/RoboVerse, worked examples include a milk-carton grasp), cost unmeasured (not present), marginal over simpler baseline (not present, tenfold).
matches.reason: Operation is: learned model emits an executable control program, interpreter/IK/PD execute it, and execution state feeds back to revise the program every K steps. The pattern is actually operated rather than mentioned. Differs from sibling-less C25 by lacking a formal verifier or solver-checked candidate selection.

rs_pattern.reason: Closest of the 15 mains is decompose_and_delegate (C25: executable intermediate artifact routed to interpreter/IK with execution feedback). adapt_via_conditioning (C03) was read and rejected as primary: it concerns a trained/unified conditioning schema with category holdout, whereas VLCP re-conditions a frozen model each block without teaching a schema; no supporting card added because no distinct second operation needs one.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: the matched K=T control and 27.3% recovery support that within-episode rewriting reduces open-loop failure in sim with privileged poses; it does not show the gap is closed against retry/monitor baselines or in real perception.

domain_pattern.unassigned: Cross-episode skill library (S2) does not satisfy K303: no mining criterion, review, success filtering or measured reuse.
revision_proposals: R05 operation says 'between trials' and 'no model in the control loop at run time'; VLCP rewrites inside an episode with the model re-entered every K steps. Consider an in-episode variant or sub-card (needs a second independent paper, e.g. CaP-Agent0).

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS C25: learned model emits an executable artifact routed to a sound executor with verifiable feedback. K105: frozen frontier model writes and runs code composing primitives, retrying locally. Both map to VLCP's VLM-written control function executed by IK/PD with state feedback.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: K105 keeps the planner in a coding runtime with persistent cells; VLCP rewrites a full policy on a fixed cadence and has no tool-call interface or success detector.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Both rewrite a whole controller program from execution evidence (trace, images).
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: R05 rewrites between trials and deploys the program without the model; VLCP rewrites within an episode and keeps the model in the loop. Differs in timing and loop locus, so the mapping is partial.

claims.text: Within-episode code replanning (K=50) drives success: 35.1% vs 3.5% for the identical open-loop system.
claims.setting: MuJoCo/RoboVerse Franka; 57 LIBERO-Object/LIBERO-90 tasks; GPT-5.5; privileged object poses
claims.selection_vs_test: no separate selection set stated; K=50 chosen without sweep
claims.result_denominator: pooled 35.1% [24.0,48.1] vs 3.5% [1.0,11.9] (counts 20/57 vs 2/57 implied by the percentages); one episode per task
claims.counterevidence: Baseline has 10x fewer calls; baseline prompt adaptation unstated; no retry/monitor/CaP baselines
claims.allowed_conclusion: In this simulator with privileged poses, adding block-wise re-observation and rewriting raised single-run success from near-zero to ~35% relative to a single-query version of the same system.

claims.text: Mechanism: 27.3% of failed grasps are recovered by a later replan.
claims.setting: 75 closed-loop pick-and-place episodes (superset of the sweep)
claims.counterevidence: Heuristic grasp-failure label and 0.13 m threshold; denominators differ from main sweep; no causal test that rewriting (vs resampling) caused recovery
claims.allowed_conclusion: Recovery events occur in a minority of failed-grasp episodes and are consistent with, not proof of, the claimed mechanism.

claims.text: The loop is cheap: ~10 queries, 84% input tokens cached.
claims.result_denominator: median 10 calls, 43k input tokens, 18.8 s latency per replan
claims.counterevidence: No USD, no compute-matched baseline; 18.8 s/replan limits control rate
claims.allowed_conclusion: Operating cost is measured and moderate for slow tabletop manipulation.

claims.text: Cross-episode skill library lets the repertoire grow without retraining.
claims.selection_vs_test: library reset per task in the sweep
claims.allowed_conclusion: The mechanism exists; its benefit is unmeasured.

claims.text: VLCP shows no phrasing dependence under instruction reframing unlike VLA-0.
claims.counterevidence: Small N; authors call it indicative
claims.allowed_conclusion: Descriptive observation at N=10; not a conclusive generalisation result.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop simulator success by environment predicate; single simulator/embodiment, development use of tasks undisclosed, no real-robot or unseen-embodiment evidence; privileged poses.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In MuJoCo/RoboVerse with privileged object poses and a strong frozen VLM, re-observing and rewriting the control function every 50 steps gave 35.1% single-run pooled success vs 3.5% for a single-query version of the same system across 57 LIBERO tasks, with recovery events logged for a minority of failed grasps.
unresolved: Is rewriting code the cause, versus more queries or resampling
Behaviour under perception noise and on a real robot
Variance across seeds and sensitivity to K
Whether the K=T baseline prompt was handicapped
assessment.reproduction_note: All results are author-reported; nothing was run by us.

G.reason: Concrete failure (silent failed-grasp propagation) with cited neighbours (one-shot code, monitor/retry, Act-Observe-Rewrite between trials) and a table locating the residue. Not 4 because the exact design point is already taken by concurrent CaP-Agent0 and neighbour full texts are not pinned.

M.reason: Two-loop argument (frozen logic inside a block vs rewrite across blocks) is clear and gives a distinguishing prediction (open-loop recovery = 0). Not 4 because 'rewrite code' vs 're-query with fresh state' vs retry is never distinguished and K is unswept.

X.reason: Prompt blocks, cadence, history truncation, skill import/revert, caching and the output contract are specified and the appendix gives verbatim contract and samples; information access (privileged poses) disclosed. Not 4 because the skill-library selection is just recency/import success, a safety fallback is referenced but not described, and transfer limits are only partly bounded.

measurement.reason: Success is an environment terminal predicate with pooled counts and CIs, but every task is a single episode with no repeats (anchor v2: single-trial -> <=2), poses are privileged, and the recovery metric is an author heuristic on a different denominator (75/81 vs 57).

causality.reason: A clean matched K=T control varying only cadence (same simulator, API, poses, tasks, model, episode budget) supports the cadence effect strongly. Held back from 4: 10x call asymmetry, no retry/monitor/CaP baselines, vision and skill library untoggled, K=T prompt adaptation unstated.

holdout.reason: Single simulator and embodiment, LIBERO tasks, no stated dev/test split for prompt or example design (worked examples overlap LIBERO objects); reframing study is small and only partially held out. Zero-demo method so no training overlap, hence not 0-1.

statistics.reason: Wilson CIs and a partial failure decomposition (40/55 unrecovered) but one episode per task, no variance across seeds, authors concede this; anchor v2 allows 1-2 for trial counts without variance.

cost.reason: Calls, tokens, cache hit, latency and code validity measured from logs; no USD and no compute-matched comparison (K=T uses one call), so budget fairness is incomplete.
